sources.title: David Tong, Applications of Quantum Mechanics, University of Cambridge lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete 370-page lecture-note PDF retrieved and inspected. §6.3.4, printed pp. 172–174: Berry connection, gauge change, loop phase, and curvature surface integral. §6.3.5, printed pp. 175–177: the two-state magnetic-field example, spinor patch behavior, monopole curvature, and Chern-number interpretation.

contents.name: §6.3.4 Berry connection, gauge change, loop phase and surface-curvature formula
contents.support: Independent check of the Abelian connection and gauge convention. Tong uses the real one-form A_T=-i<u|du> and e^{i gamma}=exp(i integral A_T); the authored convention is A=u*du with parallel coefficient c'=-A c, so signs were converted directly.

contents.name: §6.3.5 two-state spin in a magnetic field, printed pp. 175–177
contents.support: The source gives an independent spin-half monopole and solid-angle calculation for its ground-state line. The batch uses the positive eigenline, so its sign is recalculated from the displayed spinor rather than copied.

contents.name: §6.3.4–6.3.5 source curvature and phase displays
contents.support: The local theorem and example do not use the source's printed polar curvature or the adjacent surface-phase sign as premises. Direct differentiation gives F=i sin(theta)dtheta wedge dphi/2 in the anti-Hermitian convention.
contents.reason: The printed polar curvature omits the coordinate factor 1/2, and the nearby surface-phase equations have inconsistent signs. The proof supplies its own convention and calculation.

sources.title: J. E. Avron, R. Seiler, and L. G. Yaffe, Adiabatic Theorems and Applications to the Quantum Hall Effect, Communications in Mathematical Physics 110 (1987), 33–49
sources.locator: Complete 18-page article retrieved and inspected. §1, printed pp. 36–37: adiabatic evolution, the generator H_A=H+(i/tau)[P',P], and the intertwining condition. §2, printed pp. 37–43: common-domain/gap hypotheses, resolvent regularity, unitarity, Lemma 2.3 intertwining, Theorem 2.4 comparison, and Theorem 2.8 O(1/tau) leakage.

contents.name: §1 adiabatic evolution and parallel transport; §2 Lemmas 2.2–2.3
contents.support: Independent treatment of the Kato commutator generator, unitarity and intertwining for gapped spectral subspaces. The local finite-dimensional proof independently establishes the exact C2 projector-family interface.

contents.name: §2 Theorems 2.4 and 2.8 and their finite-gap comparison argument
contents.support: Independent check that slow-time leakage requires a uniform spectral gap and is O(1/tau). The authored estimate instead applies the exact current finite-matrix supplier and explicitly rescales tau=T/hbar.

contents.support: No Hall Hamiltonian, many-body transport model, or empirical claim is included in this assigned pair.
contents.reason: The scope is finite-dimensional projector geometry, a spin-half example, and a finite-matrix adiabatic estimate.
